GLOSSARY

Shared terms for a connected knowledge graph.

Only concepts used by MESA topic clusters are included; each term points back to practical and research context.

Terms used on this site

AssertionCanonical recordProjectionMutationAdmissionCOMMITTEDDLQ (dead-letter queue)PrincipalTenant · workspace · datasetACL and rolesSessionAgentRevision and chunkEmbeddingBM25RRF (reciprocal rank fusion)Validation mode (MESA_TIER3_MODE)V3 and V4MCP (Model Context Protocol)Profile BNO-GO (production status)
Assertion
One structured fact extracted from a source, written as subject → predicate → object (for example “Atlas archive → opens at → 09:00”). Every assertion points back to the text that supports it.
Canonical record
The authoritative copy of a fact, kept in SQLite. Search data in LanceDB and Kùzu is derived from it and can be rebuilt from it.
Projection
A copy of canonical data reshaped for one kind of search: vectors in LanceDB for meaning, a graph in Kùzu for relationships. Projections follow SQLite; they never decide anything.
Mutation
Any change to memory: inserting a source, correcting it, rolling it back or purging it. Each mutation has an ID and a status you can poll.
Admission
The moment MESA accepts a mutation and records it durably. The API answers 202 at admission; processing happens afterwards.
COMMITTED
The successful final state of a mutation: SQLite, LanceDB and Kùzu have all been written. Only then is the new memory fully searchable.
DLQ (dead-letter queue)
Where work goes after its retries run out. It stays there, visible, until an operator replays it. Nothing in the DLQ counts as stored memory.
Principal
The caller identity behind an API key. Roles are granted to a principal, never to a request.
Tenant · workspace · dataset
The three nested scopes data lives in. A tenant contains workspaces, a workspace contains datasets. Permissions are granted at any level and inherit downward.
ACL and roles
Who may do what. Roles are OWNER, WRITER and READER; purge and rollback need their own explicit permission on the dataset.
Session
Created by the server for one principal and one agent. It fixes which datasets can be read for its whole life; the client cannot widen it.
Agent
The AI persona or worker a session acts for. It labels context; it is not a security boundary.
Revision and chunk
A document is stored as immutable revisions; each revision is split into exact text chunks. A search result names the document, revision and chunk it came from.
Embedding
A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a text, produced by an embedding model. Query and stored embeddings must come from the same model and size.
BM25
A classic keyword ranking method. It rewards passages that contain the query’s words, especially rare ones. MESA runs it on SQLite FTS5.
RRF (reciprocal rank fusion)
A way to merge several ranked lists: each list gives a candidate 1 / (60 + its rank), and the sums are compared. It uses positions, not raw scores, and is not a probability.
Validation mode (MESA_TIER3_MODE)
How strictly extracted facts are checked before they become memory: 0 = rule-based checks, 1 = plus one model validator, 2 = two different models must agree.
V3 and V4
Two API generations in the same package. V4 is the current design with datasets, sessions and the ledger; V3 is kept only for compatibility.
MCP (Model Context Protocol)
An open protocol that lets AI tools call external services. MESA offers an MCP gateway so an agent can search and write memory within its session scope.
Profile B
The end-to-end certification scenario that moves frozen legal data from MESA Data into Core and checks every receipt. It has not passed yet.
NO-GO (production status)
The project’s own verdict that Core is not yet approved for production use. Remaining gates are listed on the status page.
